facts.claim: Operating a home care organization that provides personal care services requires a VDH home care organization (HCO) license under Code Article 7.1.
facts.value: Home care organization (HCO) license issued by VDH
facts.quote: No person shall establish or operate a home care organization without a license issued pursuant to this article
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1. Home Care Organization Licensing

facts.topic: Definition: personal care is an HCO service
facts.claim: The statutory definition of home care organization includes organizations that provide personal care services in a residence, so a private-pay personal care agency falls within the license requirement.
facts.value: Personal care services in the individual's residence are a licensable HCO service
facts.quote: Personal care services, including assistance in personal care to include activities of daily living provided in an individual's residence
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1. Home Care Organization Licensing

facts.claim: The licensure rules for home care organizations are in Virginia Administrative Code Chapter 381, not Chapter 371 (which governs nursing facilities).
facts.value: 12VAC5-381 (Regulations for the Licensure of Home Care Organizations)
facts.quote: Chapter 381. Regulations for the Licensure of Home Care Organizations
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381)

facts.claim: An HCO that is licensed and then becomes Medicare/Medicaid certified can qualify for an exemption from the licensure article, but initial state licensure is still required first.
facts.value: Exemption available only after initial licensure (certification, accreditation, or hospice license)
facts.quote: Certified by the Department of Health under provisions of Title XVIII or Title XIX of the Social Security Act
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1. Home Care Organization Licensing

facts.claim: Providers offering only homemaker, chore or companion services are outside the chapter, so a private-pay companion-only business would not need the HCO license.
facts.value: Not applicable to homemaker, chore or companion-only providers
facts.quote: this chapter is not applicable to those providers of only homemaker, chore or companion services
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381)

facts.claim: The HCO license application fee is set by regulation at $1,500 for each initial and renewal application.
facts.quote: The OLC shall collect a fee of $1,500 for each initial and renewal license application.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-70 Fees

facts.topic: When the license fee is paid and refundability
facts.claim: The license fee must accompany the application and is nonrefundable.
facts.quote: Fees shall accompany the licensure application and are not refundable.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-70 Fees

facts.claim: A 2025 fast-track rulemaking amended the HCO fee rules and changed the license term to three years and the fee to $1,500.
facts.value: Fee raised to $1,500; license term changed to three years (rule effective May 22, 2025 per LIS history)
facts.quote: increase the fee for an HCO license to $1,500
facts.title: Vol. 41 Iss. 17 (Fast-Track) 12VAC5-381 Regulations For The Licensure Of Home Care Organizations

facts.claim: A late fee applies if a renewal application is not filed by the required date.
facts.quote: An additional late fee of $50 shall be collected for an organization's failure to file a renewal application by the date specified.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-70 Fees

facts.claim: Reissuing or replacing a license carries a processing fee that accompanies the request.
facts.quote: A processing fee of $250 shall be collected for each reissuance or replacement of a license
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-70 Fees

facts.claim: A written exemption request requires a one-time processing fee submitted with the exemption application.
facts.quote: A one-time processing fee of $75 for exemption from licensure shall accompany the exemption application.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-70 Fees

facts.claim: An initial application must be filed a minimum period before the planned opening date so OLC can process it.
facts.value: At least 60 days before planned opening
facts.quote: A completed application for initial licensure must be submitted at least 60 days prior to the organization's planned opening date
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-40 License application

facts.claim: An application is complete only when all requested information and the fee are submitted; an incomplete one goes inactive after a set period.
facts.value: Inactive six months after receipt if incomplete
facts.quote: An incomplete application shall become inactive six months after it is received by the OLC.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-40 License application

facts.claim: HCO licenses expire on the third anniversary of issuance or renewal.
facts.quote: Every such license shall expire on the third anniversary of its issuance or renewal.
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1. Home Care Organization Licensing, 32.1-162.9

facts.claim: An initial applicant must prove reserve operating funds sufficient to run the organization for a defined period after licensure.
facts.value: Reserve funds covering three months of operation
facts.quote: sufficient to ensure operation of the home care organization for the three-month period after a license to operate has been issued
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-190. Financial controls

facts.claim: VDH requires an on-site survey by its Home Care Licensing staff before an initial license is issued.
facts.value: On-site survey required for initial license
facts.quote: For an initial license, an on-site survey must be conducted by the Home Care Licensing staff of the Virginia Department of Health.
facts.title: Virginia Department of Health Office of Licensure and Certification, Home Care Licensure Survey Checklist
facts.publisher: Virginia Department of Health, Office of Licensure and Certification
facts.as_of: Undated VDH guidance (predates current fee rules); verify with OLC

facts.claim: The state may inspect applicants and renewing organizations to confirm compliance.
facts.quote: The activities and services of each applicant for issuance or renewal of a home care organization license shall be subject to an inspection or examination by the Commissioner
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.9

facts.claim: Routine inspections follow a uniformly applied risk-based schedule, with extra inspections for follow-up, complaints or public safety.
facts.value: Risk-based inspection schedule plus follow-up and complaint inspections
facts.quote: required by a uniformly applied risk-based schedule established by the Department
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.10

facts.claim: The governing body must appoint an administrator with at least one year of direct health care delivery training/experience, including supervisory or administrative management experience in the last five years.
facts.value: ≥1 year direct health care delivery; ≥1 year supervisory/administrative within last 5 years
facts.quote: The governing body shall appoint as administrator an individual who has evidence of at least one year of training and experience in direct health care service delivery
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-170. Administrator

facts.claim: The administrator must be a direct employee, and one person may serve as administrator and director of nursing only if dually qualified.
facts.value: Must be employee; may combine with DON if dually qualified
facts.quote: The administrator, the director of nursing, or other clinical director may be the same individual if that individual is dually qualified.
facts.title: Documents Incorporated by Reference (12VAC5-381), 12VAC5-381-10 Definitions

facts.claim: The Board's personal care rules must provide for licensed-nurse supervision of attendants, which may be done by interactive audio or video technology.
facts.value: Supervision by licensed nurse, may use interactive audio/video
facts.quote: Regulations governing the delivery of personal care services shall provide for supervision of home care attendants providing personal care services by a licensed nurse
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.12

facts.claim: The organization must maintain a staffing plan and enough qualified staff for assessed client needs; no numeric ratio appears in the chapter.
facts.value: Sufficient numbers of qualified staff (no numeric ratio found)
facts.quote: shall provide qualified staff in sufficient numbers to meet the assessed needs of all clients
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-200. Personnel practices

facts.claim: The agency must have posted business hours and arrange on-call services around the clock.
facts.quote: the organization shall provide or arrange for services to their clients on an on-call basis 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-150. Management and administration

facts.claim: Compensated employees must receive a criminal record clearance within 30 days of hire, and staff in direct patient contact need clearance before such work unless supervised.
facts.quote: shall, within 30 days of employment, obtain for any compensated employees an original criminal record clearance
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.9:1

facts.claim: Barrier-crime convictions bar compensated employment; a misdemeanor conviction (non-abuse/neglect) allows hiring after five years.
facts.value: Barrier crimes bar hire; misdemeanor exception after 5 years
facts.quote: if five years have elapsed since the conviction
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.9:1

facts.claim: The HCO must maintain general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence plus malpractice coverage.
facts.value: ≥$1,000,000 general liability per occurrence; malpractice required
facts.quote: of at least $1 million comprehensive general liability per occurrence
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-210. Indemnity coverage

facts.topic: Crime insurance or fidelity bond minimum
facts.claim: The organization must carry third-party crime insurance or a blanket fidelity bond at a minimum amount.
facts.quote: Third-party crime insurance or a blanket fidelity bond of $50,000 minimum.
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-210. Indemnity coverage

facts.claim: Failing to keep the required liability and crime coverage leads to license revocation.
facts.quote: Failure to maintain these requirements shall result in revocation of the home care organization's license.
facts.title: Code of Virginia Article 7.1, 32.1-162.11

facts.claim: The organization must comply with local ordinances governing its operations; this is the only local-siting language found, and no specific zoning rule was located.
facts.value: Must comply with local ordinances (no specific zoning standard found)
facts.quote: Comply with federal and state laws, regulations and local ordinances governing operations of the organization
facts.title: 12VAC5-381-160. Governing body
